head: 0324fb1cc2781b7b1235932c982fba20f3e47800
headline: The app now has a health check web address that reports it is running and its version number. It is safe to ship.
what_changed: Your hosting provider can now visit a new web address, /healthz, to check that the app is up. The reply means 'I'm OK' and includes the app's version number (currently 4.1.2).
The version number is read from the app's main project file once, when the app starts, so it updates by itself with each new release.
A small automatic test was added. It checks that the health address answers and gives the right reply. The existing parcel lookup test still passes.
Parcel lookups and all other existing behaviour are unchanged.

risks.title: Anyone can see which app version you run
risks.explanation: The health address is public, so anyone who finds it can see your version number. That can help an attacker a little, because it tells them which version to look up known weaknesses for. You asked for the version, and it reveals no customer data, so this is a minor trade-off. If you don't need the version, it can be removed from the reply later.

questions_for_developer: When we publish the app, is the main project file (package.json) always copied alongside the app code? The app now reads it at startup and won't start if it is missing.
Does our hosting provider only need a 'success' reply, or does it expect the health check at a particular path or port? Please confirm /healthz on our usual port matches its settings.
good_news: The change is small and self-contained. It adds one new address and does not touch parcel lookups.
The health check takes no input from visitors and reveals no customer data.
There is now an automatic test for the health check, and the existing test still passes.
